questions: What is the exact definition of "odd cycle" - does it refer to a cycle with an odd number of edges or an odd number of vertices?
Does the game end immediately when a player cannot make a move, or do they continue playing until all possible edges are added?
Are self-loops (edges connecting a vertex to itself) allowed to be added during the game, or are they implicitly forbidden?
When checking if adding an edge creates an odd cycle, are we only considering simple cycles or all cycles including those that repeat vertices?
If the initial graph already contains all possible edges (complete graph), does the first player immediately lose or is there some other outcome?
Does "simple undirected graph" guarantee that there are no self-loops in the initial graph, or is this a separate constraint?
When two players can make equivalent optimal moves, does the tie-breaking favor the first player or second player, or is the outcome independent of such choices?
Is the winning condition determined by the total number of moves made, or by the specific sequence of moves each player makes?

You are given a simple undirected graph with N vertices and M edges, with vertices labeled 1 to N and edges labeled 1 to M. The i-th edge connects vertices U_i and V_i. This question addresses a different ambiguity not covered in the reference. Takahashi and Aoki will play a game using this graph G. With Aoki going first, they take turns performing the following operation:
- Choose a pair of integers (i,j) with 1 \leq i < j \leq N that satisfies both of the following conditions, then add an edge connecting vertices i and j to G.
- G does not already have an edge connecting vertices i and j.
- Adding an edge connecting vertices i and j does not create an odd cycle.
A player who cannot perform this operation loses, and the other player wins.
Determine who wins when both players play optimally.
Input
The input is given from Standard Input in the following format:
N M
U_1 V_1
U_2 V_2
\vdots
U_M V_M
Output
If Aoki (the first player) wins, print Aoki
Constraints
- 1 \leq N \leq 2\times 10^5
- 0 \leq M \leq 2\times 10^5
- 1 \leq U_i < V_i \leq N
- The given graph does not contain an odd cycle.
- The given graph does not contain multi-edges.
- All input values are integers.
